reason: A share in a color-mix() needs no token: tokens/contrast.json names each mix, and the contrast gate measures the color it makes.
Zero, with a unit or without, is the same length, time, angle or number in every unit, so it needs no token.

A hairline or a one-pixel step is the smallest mark a screen draws, and keeps that size at every density and shape: a rule, border, ring or outline; a 1px gap, as between a row's title and subtitle; a 1px offset of an outline or a margin, as outside an accent swatch's checked ring; and the visually hidden box.
The whole or half of a box or of the window follows the layout, so it needs no token: full width or height, 100dvh, and centering with 50% and -50%.

One of a unit is the unit itself, so it needs no token: fully opaque, one share of the free space (flex: 1, 1fr), a line box as tall as its font (line-height: 1), and one line of the element's own text (1lh, and the @supports test for it).

A sign flip, a double or a half of a token derives from it, because a token often applies to both sides of a box or to a pair: twice an inset is the inset on each side, and half of a difference is each side's share. Inside calc(), min(), max() or clamp(), it needs no token of its own.

A quarter of a token derives from it: the radius chain's floor is a quarter of radius-step, as the radius note in tokens.json defines it, so the floor follows the step. Four times a token is a new size, which is a choice, so 4 as a multiplier fails.
A quarter turn points a glyph another way, as a chevron turns when its section opens. It is a direction and has no size.
A border-radius of 999px keeps a shape round in every shape setting, square included, as status dots and the step mark are. A shape that follows the setting uses radius-capsule.
z-index 1 to 4 orders the parts of one component among themselves. Anything that layers over other components or the page uses a layer token (z-menu and the others).
A grid line number names a position, and a line clamp counts lines of text. Neither is a size.
The Checkbox's check mark and dash are drawn with borders, and these numbers are the drawing's geometry: its size, stroke, rounded end, offset and turn. A new glyph is an SVG sized with a size token.
A skeleton placeholder's widths and heights imitate the lines and rows it stands in for, and vary on purpose. Its colors, radii and spacing still come from tokens.
The skip link waits twice its own height above the page until it takes focus. The offset is a share of the link's own height, so it follows the link's size.
